subject: SKU normalization cascade causing withheld marketplace payouts

Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 23:12:00 +0530
Subject: Withheld payouts for Oct — likely due to legacy SKU IDs remap

Hi Tessa,

We noticed two withheld payout batches for October (AWS invoice #AMZ-987654 and GCP invoice #GCP-1832). Line items reference an old SKU namespace (sku_legacy_3f) that we stopped using in July — but the marketplace invoices are attributing usage to both the legacy SKU and the new SKU in the same day, producing offset/double-counted adjustments and triggering automated holdbacks.

I've attached a small manifest (suspect_usage_manifest.csv) with a sample of the affected usage rows and invoice refs. Can you confirm whether Redwood's ingestion / SKU normalization pipeline might have remapped legacy IDs back to active SKUs during the Oct 26–27 deployment window?

This is holding ~$42,000 in APAC payouts for us — need to accelerate.

Thanks,
Asha Menon
Head of Finance Ops
EdgeScale Retail

Subject: Re: Fwd: Withheld payouts for Oct — likely due to legacy SKU IDs remap

Quick summary of findings from the ingestion team: we saw a config migration on 2026-10-26 22:04 UTC that re-applied a SKU normalization profile from an older branch (deploy tag sku-normalize-v3.4.1). That profile contains legacy->canonical mapping rules, but due to a small key-format change in the normalization hash (we changed delimiter from '::' to '#'), the reconciliation join produced both the legacy and canonical keys for ~0.6% of records that contained composite meter IDs. In short: normalization produced duplicated attribution (both sku_legacy_3f and sku_edge_3f showing up).

Actions taken:
- Generated a mapping-diff snapshot and attached as sku-mapping-diff.csv (small)
- Marked the normalization job as rolled back to sku-normalize-v3.5.0 (which uses canonical-only keys) at 2026-10-27 01:12 UTC
- Running a backfill job to reprocess impacted ingestion windows (expected completion: 2026-11-01 22:00 UTC UTC)

Implication for payouts: once the backfill completes we can produce a corrected delta ledger for the marketplaces — this will be the artifact Marissa sends to payment teams. I recommend we also provide the marketplaces with a short evidence bundle (manifest + mapping diff + run logs).

Attachments: sku-mapping-diff.csv

-Karthik

Asha — update and proposed playbook below. We've confirmed the root cause (see Karthik's mapping diff). High level: a config migration reintroduced an older normalization profile that produced duplicate attribution for composite meter IDs on 10/26–10/27. Our backfill is in progress and expected to finish 2026-11-01 22:00 UTC; next actions: 

Redwood proposed playbook (timeline & owners):
1) Deliver evidence bundle (today EOD): suspect_usage_manifest.csv + sku-mapping-diff.csv + run_log_excerpt.txt (owner: Karthik)
2) Produce corrected delta ledger (Marissa) — ETA: 2026-11-02 06:00 UTC. This will be a CSV with corrected usage lines formatted for AWS/GCP ingestion APIs.
3) Marketplace hold release request (Marissa) — include evidence bundle + signed attestation + reconciled ledger. Requested SLA exception: expedited review within 5 business days.
4) Interim customer credit option: Redwood Finance (Naomi) can approve a temporary advance equal to 50% of the affected funds if marketplaces don't release within 7 business days (owner: Naomi)
5) Postmortem & preventative controls (Karthik/Jonas): harden normalization pipeline, add a pre-deploy mapping diff check, and add unit tests for delimiter changes (owner: Karthik).

Attachments: proposed-reconciliation-playbook.pdf, payout-exception-request.docx

If that works I'll have Marissa open the partner tickets and attach the evidence bundle. Please confirm whether EdgeScale wants us to file the payout-advance request now or wait until the marketplace confirms timelines.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
